extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, tribal authorities, regulated power companies/operators of fossil fuel-fired electric utility generating units (EGUs), grid operators, reliability authorities, environmental justice and community stakeholders, and legal/regulatory practitioners
extracted.subtask_short: EPA GHG standards for fossil fuel EGUs
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule preamble and guidance establishing New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and emission guidelines for greenhouse gases from fossil fuel-fired electric utility generating units, including applicability, BSER determinations, compliance timelines and flexibilities, reliability mechanisms, environmental justice considerations, and procedural/judicial review rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability flexibilities and mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For existing fossil fuel-fired EGUs, a short-term reliability emergency mechanism is available for states to provide more flexibility by using an alternative emission limitation during acute operational emergencies; a similar short-term reliability emergency mechanism is available to new sources. States may provide a reliability assurance mechanism of up to 1 year that under limited circumstances would allow existing units that had planned to cease operating by a certain date to temporarily remain available to support reliability. Any extensions exceeding 1 year must be addressed through a state plan revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features include (1) a short-term reliability mechanism to allow affected EGUs to operate at baseline emission rates during documented reliability emergencies; (2) a reliability assurance mechanism to allow states to delay cease operation dates by up to 1 year where planned retirements would disrupt reliability; (3) compliance extensions for unanticipated delays with control technology implementation. Utilization of these pathways requires an adequate demonstration of need, certification by a reliability authority, and approval by the appropriate EPA Regional Administrator. EPA plans to seek FERC advice for extension requests exceeding 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance timelines and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final compliance date for implementation of CCS for long-term coal-fired steam generating units is January 1, 2032. EPA is creating a mechanism whereby baseload new combustion turbines may request a 1-year extension of their CCS compliance deadline under certain circumstances. States may provide for a compliance date extension for existing sources of up to 1 year under certain circumstances for sources installing control technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized longer compliance timelines in response to comments; an administrative mechanism allows extensions of up to 1 year for unforeseen circumstances outside an owner/operator's control (e.g., supply chain challenges or permitting delays). Any extensions over 1 year must be handled through a state plan revision. EPA also emphasizes the need for transparent unit-specific compliance information so grid operators can plan for changes with greater certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) statutory criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of the BSER is made based on consideration of the statutory criteria, including emission reductions, cost, energy requirements, and non-air health and environmental considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized that CCS is the BSER for certain subcategories of new and existing EGUs based on evaluation of these criteria. The preamble references consideration of all statutory factors when selecting the BSER and explains that uncertainties in any of the statutory evaluation criteria can preclude designation of a pathway as part of BSER (e.g., low-GHG hydrogen co-firing was not finalized as a BSER pathway due to identified uncertainties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology neutrality and voluntary use of non-BSER technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 111, EPA establishes standards of performance but does not mandate use of any particular technology to meet those standards; sources may elect to use technologies that are not designated as BSER pathways for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although EPA did not finalize low-GHG hydrogen co-firing as a BSER pathway, certain sources may still elect to co-fire hydrogen for compliance. The preamble explains the distinction between setting standards and mandating technology, and clarifies that non-BSER technologies remain potential compliance options at the source's election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice (EJ) considerations and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must carefully consider impacts of these actions on communities with environmental justice concerns, including potential health, environmental, and safety impacts of CCS and the potential for localized increases in emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency conducted extensive outreach with Tribal nations and EJ communities and incorporated feedback into final actions. EPA analyzed distributional air quality and public health impacts (documented in the RIA and preamble sections) and expects states to conduct meaningful engagement. EPA will consider CEQ CCUS guidance, coordinate among federal/state/tribal regulators, and review NSR permitting and BACT determinations specifically with respect to GHGs and co-pollutant increases to reduce risks to historically disadvantaged communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful engagement requirements in state plans
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include requirements for meaningful engagement in development of state plans, including with energy workers, communities living near EGUs, workers involved in installing pollution control technology, and organizations representing these workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA expects states to include a wide range of stakeholders as part of constructive engagement under the rule's requirements so that community members adversely impacted by pollution, energy workers, consumers, and other interested parties can have their concerns heard when states make decisions about standards of performance, compliance strategies, and compliance flexibilities for existing EGUs. EPA consulted the Federal Interagency Working Group on Coal and Power Plant Communities and Economic Revitalization (Energy Communities IWG) in developing these engagement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan responsibilities and mechanisms under emission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The emission guidelines in 40 CFR part 60, subpart UUUUb are for states to follow in developing, submitting, and implementing state plans to establish performance standards to reduce GHGs from designated existing sources; states determine future operations of EGUs within their jurisdiction and may include reliability mechanisms and compliance flexibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States are responsible for weighing input from stakeholders and considering multiple factors in determining operations and compliance approaches. State plans may incorporate the EPA's reliability instruments (short-term emergency mechanism, compliance date extensions, reliability assurance mechanism). If a state includes mechanisms that extend operations or compliance beyond certain limits (e.g., >1 year), those changes generally require a state plan revision. Under the Tribal Authority Rule, tribes may seek approval to implement plans similar to states (TIP); if a tribe does not obtain authority, EPA may establish a Federal plan for facilities in Indian country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability based on construction/reconstruction dates and NAICS codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Final amendments to 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT apply to affected facilities that began construction after January 8, 2014 but before May 23, 2023; NSPS codified in subpart TTTTa apply to facilities that begin construction, reconstruction, or modification on or after May 23, 2023. Emission guidelines in subpart UUUUb apply to 'existing sources' as defined in CAA section 111(a)(6). The NAICS codes for the source category are 221112 and 921150.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed NAICS codes are illustrative and not exhaustive. The emission guidelines would not apply to EGUs that are new after January 8, 2014, or reconstructed after June 18, 2014, per the stated applicability dates. Tribes can pursue TIP approval under 40 CFR part 49, subpart A; otherwise a Federal plan may apply to Indian country facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization and cessation-by exemptions for coal-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not finalizing the proposed imminent-term (cease operation prior to Jan 1, 2032) and near-term (cease operation prior to Jan 1, 2035) subcategories for existing coal-fired steam generating units; instead EPA finalized an applicability exemption for units demonstrating they plan to permanently cease operation before January 1, 2032.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal originally included four subcategories distinguishing units by operating horizon and load. Commenters requested changes to dates and utilization limits. EPA responded by removing the imminent-term and near-term subcategories and adopting a cease-operation-by exemption for units planning permanent cessation before the specified date. See section VII.B for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource adequacy and reliability analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA evaluated resource adequacy implications in a final technical support document and conducted capacity expansion modeling of the final rules in a manner that takes into account resource adequacy needs, concluding that resource adequacy can be maintained with the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA modeled a scenario that complies with the final rules and meets resource adequacy needs and performed sensitivity analyses for higher electricity demand (load growth) and impacts of other pending power sector rules. These analyses indicate available industry pathways to comply while respecting NERC reliability considerations and constraints. EPA also consulted with DOE (via a March 9, 2023 MOU) and FERC expert staff during rule development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of unit-specific compliance information
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing a requirement for transparent unit-specific compliance information for EGUs to allow grid operators to plan for system changes with greater certainty and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent unit-level data on compliance timelines and plans is intended to assist balancing authorities and grid operators in system planning and reliability analyses. This transparency is listed as a reliability-supporting feature of the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial and administrative review procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review of these final actions is available only by filing a petition for review in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit by July 8, 2024. Under CAA section 307(d)(7)(B), only objections raised with reasonable specificity during the public comment period may be raised during judicial review, with a limited mechanism for reconsideration if the objection could not practicably have been raised during the comment period or arose after the period but within the time for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To seek reconsideration the person must demonstrate it was impracticable to raise the objection within the comment period or that grounds for the objection arose after the period (but within the judicial review time) and be of central relevance to the outcome. Petitions for Reconsideration should be submitted to the Office of the Administrator with copies to listed contacts and the Associate General Counsel for the Air and Radiation Law Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of local non-GHG impacts and demographic distribution of air quality effects
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA analyzes and must consider how emission changes associated with compliance scenarios affect emissions of non-GHG health-harming pollutants (NOx, SO2, PM2.5) and how air quality impacts are distributed geographically and across demographic groups, with focus on communities with EJ concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's national-level analysis (RIA and preamble sections) finds nationwide reductions in NOx, SO2, and PM2.5, but recognizes potential for localized increases in emissions where units installing CCS operate more hours or for longer periods. EPA expects states to weigh multiple factors and use meaningful engagement to reduce risks of localized increases. EPA will review and update guidance on NSR permitting, specifically BACT determinations for GHGs and co-pollutant considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination and use of external guidance (CEQ, DOE, FERC, NERC)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's consideration of CCS, reliability, and environmental protections is informed by CEQ CCUS guidance, consultations with DOE (including an MOU), FERC expert staff, and interactions with NERC and other reliability authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA recognizes that multiple federal agencies, as well as state and tribal governments, share responsibility for regulating and permitting CCS projects. The Agency will coordinate with these entities, use CEQ guidance on CCUS, consult FERC about long extensions, and seek input from reliability experts to ensure regulatory measures protect public health and grid reliability.
